policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders a plural: "for the children of Israel his companions". The qere חֲבֵרָיו is plural "his companions"; the ketiv חברו is singular "his companion". English number distinguishes the two, so the qere is selected. The mapped note is classed alternative_rendering ("Or, of") and bears only on the English wording of the preposition, not on the reading.

ASV renders a plural at the second occurrence too: "for all the house of Israel his companions". The qere חֲבֵרָיו is plural, the ketiv חברו singular; the English plural selects the qere. The note "Or, of" is an alternative_rendering and does not touch the reading.

ASV reads "the tribes of Israel his companions" — plural, matching the qere חֲבֵרָיו against the singular ketiv חברו. The mapped note is classed alternative_rendering and concerns how the following clause is phrased in English, so it does not bear on this unit.

The only variation is Hebrew verb number: plural qere יִהְיוּ against singular ketiv יהיה. The subject is plural either way ("they ... two nations"), and English requires a plural verb with a plural subject regardless of Hebrew agreement, so "they shall be no more two nations" is the natural rendering of both. No italicized supply and no mapped textual_variant note distinguishes them; the qere base fallback carries the projection.
